_note: Every fact below was retrieved from a live web search on 2026-08-08 and is cited to a primary source. This file exists so the RAG pipeline has a real, grounded example dataset to demonstrate against without requiring live internet access at run time. Nothing here is invented — see 'source_url' on each fact.

facts.statement: The ECB raised its deposit facility rate by 25bps to 2.25% (from 2.00%) effective 17 June 2026 — its first hike in three years, reversing the cutting cycle described in the March 2026 Catella report.
facts.source_name: European Central Bank — Monetary policy decision
facts.driver: Inflation pressure from an energy price shock tied to the Middle East conflict, pushing the ECB's 2026 headline inflation projection to 2.6%

facts.statement: The ECB held rates unchanged at its 23 July 2026 meeting: deposit facility 2.25%, main refinancing 2.40%, marginal lending 2.65%.
facts.source_name: European Central Bank — Economic Bulletin Issue 5, 2026

facts.statement: The US Federal Reserve held its federal funds target range at 3.50%-3.75% at its 29 July 2026 meeting, with three FOMC members dissenting in favor of a hike. This was under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
The Bank of England's MPC voted 6-3 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75% at its meeting ending 29 July 2026; the three dissenters voted for a hike to 4%, citing energy-shock inflation risk.
facts.source_name: Bank of England — Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes, July 2026

facts.statement: The European Commission estimates the EU needs to add roughly 650,000 dwellings per year on top of the 1.6 million currently built annually to close the housing supply-demand gap over the next decade, at an estimated cost of EUR 150 billion per year.
facts.source_name: European Commission — Affordable Housing Plan, Staff Working Document SWD 2025-1053-2

facts.statement: By 2035, more than 2 million new homes per year will be needed EU-wide to meet demand, implying a cumulative shortfall of 7.14 million dwellings beyond the 17.06 million units already planned.
Average house prices across the EU have risen more than 60% and rents more than 20% over the past decade; an estimated 42 million Europeans cannot afford to adequately heat their homes.
The ECB cut rates eight times from June 2024 to June 2025, then held rates unchanged from June 2025 until the June 2026 hike.
facts.source_name: UK House of Commons Library — Interest rates and monetary policy briefing
